implemented: One immutable actor-scoped operation key per original uploader/held attempt. Exact same-key confirmation returns the original timestamp/receipt; a changed key, foreign actor, reused same-actor key on another attempt or changed review intent is refused.

The attempt stays review_required, retains its content/path/review/hold identity, and remains counted by unresolved admission. Existing held rows are not backfilled with invented claims. Default READ COMMITTED unclaimed registration remains available.

Before UPDATE/DELETE guards freeze claimed attempt rows and all claim-row changes, including ordinary owner DML. The attempt mutation guard rejects stronger transaction snapshots so a previously established snapshot cannot miss a newly committed claim.

Original-actor/current explicit editing RLS applies to claim reads. No direct mutation, anonymous/service RPC or claim-table read grants. Owner management alone gives no authority. Access is rechecked after the attempt lock wait.

Replay installs after all twelve prior proposals; catalog assertions cover RLS, enabled guards, fixed function paths and narrow execution/table grants. CI trigger paths now include all five recent upload proposals on both push and pull request.

limits: Unapplied database proposal only. No app caller, UI, hosted schema, account, permission relationship, provider, file or object metadata is changed.
This pins the held attempt/claim row protocol. It does not fence physical object-store writes, trusted Storage maintenance, processing jobs, all references or the complete permission graph.

Attempt UPDATE/DELETE now requires READ COMMITTED even for unclaimed rows; unsupported stronger modes fail closed. Current default READ COMMITTED lifecycle is exercised; future callers/maintenance must account for this restriction.
Freeze guards cover ordinary row UPDATE/DELETE, not a privileged database owner disabling/altering guards or using DDL/TRUNCATE. Ordinary auth/anon/service roles get no such table mutation grant.

Claims do not expire or free quota/content uniqueness. There is no takeover, terminal release, retry, registration, byte/metadata verification, deletion, processing launch or cleanup authority in the receipt. A lost original operation key requires separately reviewed recovery; no new key can silently adopt the claim.

Actual immutable-version provider behavior, reference/retention writer inventory, exact receipts and independent physical absence proof remain open. The existing paths-only delete SDK remains insufficient for automatic cleanup.

Disposable roles use actual explicit access helpers with narrow organization/audience stubs; no hosted seven-role/browser acceptance is certified. App fingerprint excludes SQL; proposal SHA and exact-source CI remain separate proof.
